chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

It was the supplication of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on the night of the Confederates (Al-Ahzaab): 'O the Crier/Helper of the distressed, and O the Answerer of the call of the desperate, and O the Remover of my sorrow! Remove from me my sorrow, and my worry, and my distress, for indeed You know my state and the state of my companions, and Suffice me against the terror of my enemies.'

key_terms.صَرِيخَ: The Crier or Helper who responds to calls for help
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْأَحْزَابِ: The night of the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwat al-Ashab)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of the Prophet (peace be upon him) for relief from distress and worry?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) reliance on divine aid during the critical night of the Battle of the Confederates, a moment of intense psychological strain for the Muslim community. It emphasizes Allah’s attributes as the 'Cryer of the Distressed' and 'Answerer of the Desperate,' reflecting the Shia tradition of seeking intercession through the Prophet’s example during times of collective and personal tribulation. The invocation underscores the theological principle that divine knowledge of one’s state precedes the removal of grief, reinforcing trust in Allah’s timely intervention.
